problem.title: Excessive Foreign Key Cascading Deletes Locking Parent & Child Tables
problem.prompt: Customer account deletion service executing 'DELETE FROM users WHERE id = 101' configured with 'ON DELETE CASCADE'.
requirements: Operational Invariant: "Avoid multi-table synchronous cascading deletes in high-throughput OLTP systems; use soft deletes and batch pruning."
Production Hardening: Eliminate un-indexed foreign key cascades. Implement soft deletes ('is_deleted = true') or perform asynchronous background cleanup of child records in small, indexed batches.
Prevent cascading failure by isolating downstream degradation at the ingress boundary.
constraints: Incident Scenario Baseline: Customer account deletion service executing 'DELETE FROM users WHERE id = 101' configured with 'ON DELETE CASCADE'.
Failure Cascade Path: 50k Mut. → Row X-Lock → Spinlock Thrash → Deadlock Graph → 💥 DB Freeze
Sub-millisecond rejection / shed latency for overloaded requests

referenceMaterial.summary: Failure physics analysis: 50k Mut. → Row X-Lock → Spinlock Thrash → Deadlock Graph → 💥 DB Freeze.
failureModes: Cascading Failure: The cascade traverses 15 child tables containing millions of rows without indexes on foreign key columns. InnoDB acquires exclusive row and table locks across the entire database schema for 45 seconds, blocking all normal traffic.
Breakdown Chain: 50k Mut. → Row X-Lock → Spinlock Thrash → Deadlock Graph → 💥 DB Freeze
Shedding Failure: Without fast rejection at the boundary, queued dead work triggers multi-second GC pauses, CPU thrashing, and cascading 504 Gateway Timeouts.
